digest.component_or_area: op-cert service signing and key provisioning
propositions: Op-cert service currently performs per-job boto3/SSM/region lookup and patches process-global key/principal/push state, coupling app config to one secret store and allowing jobs to observe different keys.

Key and principal must be read at startup from exactly one of REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY, validated and copied to a process-owned 0700/0600 directory/file before queue/worker/network/workspace creation, with the process never rereading from the deployment source.

Both out-of-opcert_service signing producer chains (completion via transition_close.sign_completion_verdict and plan-review via generation.sign_manifest/attest.py) must accept and forward an optional context-local OpcertSigner binding, proving isolation and preventing environment patching from silently breaking either path.

The op-cert application runtime must have no SSM/boto3/region/key-parameter dependency; the compose service must materialize the key outside the app via fetch-secrets.sh to a 0600 :ro-mounted file with REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH, and the shared /rebar/prod/* SSM grant in iam.tf is deliberately unchanged.
Concurrent and timed-out jobs must prove context-local signer/principal/push isolation, one immutable startup signer, existing signature verification, and no workspace push remote.
Key material must be absent from repr, serialization, argv, logs, exceptions, output, fingerprints, provenance, children, and persisted envelopes beyond the public signature.
